title: Hillsborough County School Board, District 6 (countywide runoff)
what_it_does: School board members set the district budget and school millage, hire and evaluate the superintendent, approve curriculum materials, and set district policy.
verified_ballot_note: Runoff per Tampa Bay Times/WUSF snippets (Sally Harris Williamson eliminated). Nonpartisan.

candidates.name: Karen Perez
candidates.photo_source: Ballotpedia candidate photo (downloaded copy in assets/photos)
candidates.occupation: Licensed clinical social worker; president of Embracing Changes for Wellness, LLC
candidates.background: Perez was first elected to the countywide District 6 seat in 2018. She is a licensed clinical social worker and small-business owner who has worked in mental health, family services, veterans' care and juvenile justice probation. She led the Aug. 18, 2026 primary with about 48% and faces Kenneth Gay in the Nov. 3 runoff.

school_books.summary: In a Keep Florida Reading questionnaire, Perez said parents have a right to be involved in what their own child reads but that one parent's preference should not determine what is available to every family. She said challenged materials should be judged as a whole by qualified educators under district policy and state law, and opposed automatically posting every challenge with only a title and author.
school_books.quote: One family's objection should be heard and respected, but it should not automatically determine what other families and students may choose to access.

sources.title: Keep Florida Reading 2026 school board candidate questionnaire - Karen Perez

school_safety.summary: At a July 2026 candidate forum Perez, a clinical social worker, said student behavior problems should be looked at differently and stressed meeting students' mental-health needs before situations escalate.
school_safety.quote: we could have a different look at what's happening

candidates.name: Kenneth Gay
candidates.occupation: Retired educator (teacher, instructional leader and assistant principal, Hillsborough County Public Schools)
candidates.background: Gay retired in 2022 after 39 years with Hillsborough County Public Schools as a teacher, instructional leader and assistant principal, and holds a doctorate in child and youth studies. He ran unsuccessfully for the District 5 seat in 2024 and took about 27% in the Aug. 18, 2026 District 6 primary, advancing to the Nov. 3 runoff. He now mentors teachers and teaches student health and safety programs.

taxes.summary: At a July 2026 forum Gay said the district should 'fund the basics' rather than add new programs and should find places to cut and recycle money; he did not call for cutting taxes or the school millage.

school_books.summary: In a Keep Florida Reading questionnaire, Gay said parents should have the primary role in guiding what their own children read and offered a personal 'litmus test' about age-appropriateness, but said removal decisions should run through Hillsborough's structured review process under Florida Statute 1006.28 and be posted publicly, not driven by individual preference.
school_books.quote: Decisions should be based on established law, professional review, and district policy—not politics, public pressure, or individual preference.

sources.title: Keep Florida Reading 2026 school board candidate questionnaire - Kenneth 'Ken' Gay

school_safety.summary: Gay has pointed to what he calls a lack of consistent enforcement of student behavior rules and says classrooms need consistent consequences; his campaign site says schools should maintain discipline and clear expectations. He has not proposed adding police officers.
school_safety.quote: Students learn best in safe and structured environments where expectations are clear.

sources.title: Hillsborough County School Board candidates tackle district challenges

other_issues.title: Teacher support
other_issues.summary: His campaign site says strong schools start with educators who feel supported and respected and that teachers and staff should have what they need in the classroom, without naming pay as a top budget priority.
